summary: SRI's Artificial Intelligence group reports plans to join the ARPANET after switching their PDP-10 to TENEX. The connection would go through the existing IMP at SRI and a PDP-15 controller, using TENEX network software where possible. A response to RFC 116.

eli5.summary: A research group says here is how and when we plan to plug in to the network, and what equipment we will use.

subtitle: SRI's Artificial Intelligence group announces plans to join the ARPANET

tldr.problem: SRI's AI research group is converting to new hardware and wants to connect to the ARPANET to share research software.
tldr.mechanism: The group is migrating from a PDP-10 to a TENEX system, using a PDP-15 controller for peripherals, and will connect through an IMP. They plan to use as much existing TENEX network software as possible.
tldr.outcome: Connection target is mid-July 1971. SRI will offer AI software like QA3.6 (theorem proving) and STRIPS (problem solving) to the network.

facts.label: Main AI software
facts.value: QA3.6 theorem prover, STRIPS solver, QA4

today: RFC 152 is a status report from May 1971. SRI's AI group did connect to the ARPANET and became a notable source of AI research tools accessible over the network. The report marks an early milestone in connecting research facilities to the growing ARPANET.

sections.title: Converting to TENEX
sections.content: The Stanford Research Institute's Artificial Intelligence Group (SRAI) is replacing its current PDP-10 with a new PDP-10 running TENEX, an operating system developed at BBN. A PDP-15 will serve as a peripheral controller. The hardware interface to the IMP is in procurement. The group plans to use the existing TENEX network software, changing only the lowest-level hardware-dependent parts of the NCP (Network Control Program).
sections.eli5: We are getting new computers running TENEX and will plug them into the network using the existing software wherever we can.

sections.title: Network Services and Participation
sections.content: The most optimistic estimate for functional connection is mid-July 1971. SRI can support several simultaneous users on a system that runs during business hours and often at other times. The AI group offers research software including QA3.6 (a first-order resolution theorem prover), STRIPS (an extra-logical problem solver), and possibly QA4 (a language for problem-solving strategies). The group also seeks access to other sites' AI programs on a trial basis and occasional contact with network participants.
sections.eli5: We will be ready mid-July and can serve a few users at a time. We are sharing our AI software and want to try other people's.

sections.title: System Status
sections.content: The conversion effort is underway. System support work is currently focused on accommodating hardware and design changes. The group's participation in the Network Working Group has been minimal so far, but the authors expect it to increase as the system comes up. The report is framed as a response to RFC 116, which solicited status reports from interested ARPANET sites.
sections.eli5: We are busy getting the hardware working. When we are ready, we will join the network meetings and share what we learn.
